newsitem.title: UK: Newspapers' share of adspend continues to fall.
newsitem.headline: Newspapers' share of adspend continues to fall.

text.p: Newspapers' share of advertising expenditures continues to fall in the world's top five economies, but growth in emerging markets in Asia-Pacific and Latin America is underpinning the demand for newsprint, according to a new report.

Zenith Media, the media planning and buying unit of advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc, reported in its report, World Press Trends 1997, that the demand for newspapers is falling in the five largest economies: U.S., Japan, Germany, France and Britain.
"Newspapers are losing share of their advertising markets, principally to television, while circulations are falling as consumers find alternative ways of filling their time," Zenith said.

"In stark contrast to newspapers in mature economies, titles in emerging markets reap the benfits as rising prosperity brings with it rising readerships," Zenith said. Newspapers are the preferred advertising medium in emerging markets for high-ticket goods, Zenith said.
The demand for newsprint is forecast to rise in 1997, and with it the price of newsprint, Zenith said.

The share of advertising expenditure held by newspapers in the top five economies fell to 35.2 percent in 1996 from 38.6 percent in 1989. Newspapers' loss of share, however, is expected to decelerate in these five economies to stand at 34.2 percent in 1999, Zenith said.
"Electronic media, much heralded as the successor to print, have shown few signs of attracting a significant share of marketing spend," Zenith said.

Newspaper expenditure in emerging markets in Asia-Pacific nearly doubled to $9.5 billion in 1996 from $5.6 billion in 1993. But newspapers' share of adspend fell to 37.5 percent in 1996 from 39.8 percent in 1993, Zenith said.
Zenith expects newspaper ad spend in emerging Asia-Pacific to rise to $12.9 billion by 1999, accounting for 33.7 percent of the region's total adspend.
Denmark was the heaviest user of newspaper advertising in 1996 at 70 percent, followed by Norway at 61 percent, and Switzerland and Finland at 57 percent each, Zenith said.
